findings.title: retryCount-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany at the top of the handler now has an OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and no `scheduled: false`) filter, unlike the sibling branch. `retryCount` is a column on the shared WorkflowReminder model for all methods (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP), so this SMS cron endpoint will delete any workflow reminder row of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this endpoint writes retryCount, but the schema change makes the field available to every reminder type, and any other writer (e.g. a future WhatsApp/email retry mechanism, or manual data fixes) would have its rows silently destroyed by the SMS cron. The condition should be constrained to `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).

findings.title: retryCount incremented via read-modify-write instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both the failure branch (line 184) and the catch block (line 195) update retryCount with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read at the start of the loop. If two cron invocations overlap, or the same reminder is processed concurrently, one increment is lost, so the reminder is retried more times than the intended two before deletion. Prisma supports an atomic form: `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`, which avoids the stale-read problem entirely.

findings.title: Reminders skipped for empty message or missing sendTo never increment retryCount and retry forever
findings.body: The retry-count logic only runs inside `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`. When the message resolves to empty/null (e.g. no reminderBody and a non-REMINDER template) or `sendTo` is missing (e.g. the booking has no smsReminderNumber and the action is not SMS_NUMBER), neither the success nor the failure branch executes: the reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and is picked up again on every cron run until scheduledDate passes. This is exactly the endless-retry behavior the PR description says it is fixing, but for the 'silently skipped' class of failures. The else-branch (or an outer else) should also bump retryCount so these reminders are eventually cleaned up.

findings.title: Failed reminders are hard-deleted, losing audit trail and referenceIds
findings.body: Once a reminder exceeds the retry budget it is removed with `deleteMany`, which destroys the row including workflowStepId, bookingUid and any referenceId. There is no record that a reminder was attempted and abandoned, so neither support nor the booking owner can tell that an SMS reminder was dropped (e.g. due to an invalid phone number), and the failure reason is only available in server console logs. Consider marking the row (e.g. a status/needsAction flag) or logging the deleted reminder ids before removal, rather than silently deleting.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry-count and deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR adds a new state machine (retryCount incremented on Twilio failure or thrown error, rows deleted when retryCount > 1, deletion query rewritten as an OR) but ships no unit or integration tests. Worth covering at minimum: (1) a reminder whose scheduleSMS throws twice is deleted on the following run, (2) a reminder that succeeds after one failure is not deleted, (3) the deleteMany does not remove EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders, and (4) reminders skipped due to missing sendTo do not loop forever.
